newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian parliament approves pension increase.
newsitem.headline: Croatian parliament approves pension increase.

text.p: The Croatian parliament on Friday approved a cut in health contributions from pensions, a plan proposed by the government to improve pensioners' income, the state news agency Hina reported.
Contributions for national health care will be 18 percent with effect from January instead of 25 percent previously.
The government faces increasing pressure by pensioners and other pressure groups to do something about declining living standards ahead of the March local elections.
Croatia's social welfare minister said last week that pensions may increase by anything up to 22 percent this year.
Although their income was recently raised 10 percent across the board to an average 1,000 kuna ($180) a month, pensioners find it hard to survive.
They were outraged when the state-run pension fund said earlier this month it would delay payments due to a cash flow problem. Its director was sacked by the government last week.

Pensioners have felt the government freeze on income in its drive to stabilise the economy in the past three years more than working people and they staged mass protests last November to demand a "life of dignity".
